hindcast.verdict: Pre-registered test: model AUC 0.843 vs 0.862 (thin ice) and 0.918 (ice-edge distance). Post-hoc diagnosis: the growth-only part of the model (mid-May thickness minus survival thickness) scores 0.931, beating both; multiplying by drift retention (0.786 alone) pulls it down, because retention scores whether a cell's ice stays, not whether the cell has ice. A climatology of past Septembers scores 0.956, better than all of them.

era5_arco.dataset: ERA5 hourly reanalysis (2 m temperature analysis; snowfall 1-h accumulations from 06/18 UTC forecasts), ARCO-ERA5 copy
era5_arco.url: https://storage.googleapis.com/gcp-public-data-arco-era5/co/ (single-level-reanalysis.zarr-v2 t2m, single-level-forecast.zarr-v2 sf); ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3 for the ERA5T tail
era5_arco.doi: 10.24381/cds.adbb2d47 (ERA5 hourly single levels); Hersbach et al. 2020, QJRMS, 10.1002/qj.3803; ARCO-ERA5: Carver & Merose 2023
era5_arco.licence: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) licence / CC-BY 4.0 (ERA5); contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information. ARCO-ERA5 copy by Google Research, distributed under the same terms.
era5_arco.notes: Partial HTTP range reads of blosc block 0 of the co/ N320 stores (points north of 45N), lowest mantissa byte set to midpoint (max error 0.0033 K). T2m: daily mean of 00+12 UTC analyses 1 Nov-15 May; 16 May-15 Sep one analysis/day alternating 00/12 UTC (winter 2024 summer at 2/day). co t2m chunks for Aug 2026 were missing (store attrs claim ERA5T to 2026-10-31); those 31 hours and 1-17 Nov 2026 came from ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3 (rows 90-45N, bilinear). Snowfall: 1-h accumulations; daily = 24 x one hourly value with the valid hour rotating through 24 h. Total ERA5 transfer about 1.38 GB (all runs incl. checks) over ~60k range requests, single thread, identified UA. ERA5T preliminary after 2026-06-30. Known: ERA5 2 m temperature warm bias over sea ice in cold conditions (Wang et al. 2019, The Cryosphere 13, 1661-1679).

thickness_petty.notes: Only the listed variables were read via HTTP Range requests, every 3rd day of each month (days 1,4,...,28); no full-file downloads. Monthly mean = mean of those days.

h0.meaning: Satellite ice thickness in November, averaged across the products available that winter.
h0.why: Thin start-of-winter ice needs more growth, or help, to reach a thickness that lasts the summer.
h0.not_proof_of: Exact thickness: radar thickness depends on assumed snow depth and density, and early-winter retrievals are biased.
h0.example: November 2024: median 0.85 m in the Beaufort vs 1.96 m north of Greenland (products: cpom, petty).

disagree.meaning: Mean absolute difference between thickness products in the same cell and month.
disagree.why: Where products disagree, every downstream number is less certain; the spread feeds the ensemble.
disagree.not_proof_of: Which product is right. Disagreement only shows where to distrust them all.
disagree.example: Median disagreement across overlapping winters: 0.51 m.

fdd.meaning: Freezing degree days, 1 Nov - 15 May: how cold and how long the winter is (ERA5 climatology).
fdd.why: Cold drives natural growth and the extra growth flooding unlocks.
fdd.not_proof_of: Growth itself. ERA5 is warm-biased over sea ice in cold conditions (Wang et al. 2019), so FDD is likely low.
fdd.example: Central Arctic (>85N) median 3,425 K day; near Cambridge Bay 3,794 K day.

hs.meaning: Thickness needed by mid-May to last the melt season: melt rate x melt days (van Dijke et al. 2022 regimes).
hs.why: The finish line every cell is measured against.
hs.not_proof_of: A measured threshold. It blends two regional melt regimes by latitude; the weakest assumption in the atlas.
hs.example: Beaufort median 1.48 m vs central Arctic 0.79 m.

R.meaning: Share of ice seeded in a cell on 1 November still in ice-covered water on 15 September (OSI SAF drift).
R.why: Thickened ice that drifts out of the Arctic is lost, however thick it is.
R.not_proof_of: Multi-year retention. Summer drift is partly model-filled; 75 km drift vs 25 km cells.
R.example: Fram Strait 0.00 vs north of Greenland 0.93 (mean over years).

gap.meaning: Cells where thickening raises the survival probability by at least the threshold (default 0.2).
gap.why: This is where thickening could change the outcome, not where ice survives anyway or is hopeless.
gap.not_proof_of: A place to deploy. No ecology, community consent or logistics are included.
gap.example: 2024/25: band 11,250 km2 (1% of Real Ice's 1,000,000 km2/yr target).

sept_freq.meaning: Fraction of Septembers 2012-2025 with ice (concentration >= 15%) in the cell (OSI SAF).
sept_freq.why: Cells that flip between years are where a nudge could matter; the hindcast tests the band against them.
sept_freq.not_proof_of: That ice in that cell came from that cell: ice moves.
sept_freq.example: 22% of ice-capable cells were ice-covered in 20-80% of Septembers.

excluded.meaning: Cells within 50 km of a settlement or a hand-drawn shipping corridor (approximate, not ASTD).
excluded.why: Operations near people and ships need consent and coordination.
excluded.not_proof_of: Safety elsewhere. Indigenous use areas and ringed seal habitat are not in open data: community consent required.
excluded.example: 988,750 km2 flagged; 2,500 km2 of the 2024/25 band falls inside.

uplift.meaning: P(survive with thickening) minus P(survive without), from 1,000 Monte Carlo draws per cell.
uplift.why: Ranks cells by what thickening changes, not by how thin they are.
uplift.not_proof_of: That thickening works at scale: the gain prior comes from one 1 km site, 2024/25.
uplift.example: Gain prior: triangular 0 / 0.32 / 0.70 m, scaled by cold.

p_without.meaning: Probability the cell's ice is thick enough by mid-May to last the summer and stays in the Arctic, with no intervention.
p_without.why: The baseline every thickening scenario is measured against; this is what the hindcast tests.
p_without.not_proof_of: A forecast for one summer: it uses climatological weather, not the coming season's.

p_with.meaning: The same probability with a flooding gain added wherever start ice is at least 0.6 m.
p_with.why: Its gap to P(without) is the uplift that defines the band.
p_with.not_proof_of: That the gain is achievable everywhere: it is extrapolated from one site by how cold each cell is.

calibration.meaning: Two-stage growth model at Cambridge Bay, scaled by one factor alpha to the 2024/25 field result.
calibration.why: Ties the growth physics to the only published thickening experiment.
calibration.not_proof_of: Accuracy at 25 km: one 1 km site, one winter, approximate coordinates.
calibration.example: Uncalibrated difference 26 cm vs paper 32 cm; alpha = 1.00.

hindcast.meaning: Does P(survive without) predict where ice is present the next September, 2012-2025?
hindcast.why: A band drawn from a model that cannot hindcast would be decoration.
hindcast.not_proof_of: Skill for thickened ice: no thickened ice exists at this scale to test against.
hindcast.example: AUC model 0.843 vs thin-ice 0.862 vs ice-edge distance 0.918; growth-only component 0.931 (post hoc).

sensitivity.meaning: Band area recomputed with each input pushed low and high, one at a time.
sensitivity.why: Shows which assumption the answer leans on.
sensitivity.not_proof_of: Interactions between inputs; one-at-a-time misses them.

scale.meaning: Band area against Real Ice's scale plan: energy at 8 MWh/km2, fleet from an assumed drone throughput.
scale.why: Tests whether the plan's 1,000,000 km2/yr fits where thickening matters.
scale.not_proof_of: Feasibility. Drone throughput is not public: the fleet number is an assumption.
